method: Two independent countdown clocks sharing one state machine, timed from a monotonic clock so the display cannot drift. Pressing the running clock freezes it, banks the move, adds the Fischer increment to the opponent and starts the opponent's clock; pressing the idle clock is ignored, and the first move belongs to White. The remaining time is measured in milliseconds and shown as m:ss, switching to tenths of a second below ten seconds so the flag is visible; a clock reaching zero stops the game and marks that side as flagged, and the opponent wins on time. Pause freezes the running clock and resume restarts it without losing time; reset returns both clocks to the configured control. The increment is added at the start of a turn, so a clock may briefly show more than its starting time. Time controls of 1-180 minutes and 0-60 seconds of increment are accepted and lock once the game starts. This is a timing aid only: the insufficient-material draw on time, illegal moves, move legality and tournament rules are not evaluated.
